title: Sideband control path: a JSON/CLI way to drive every mimid action (create room, add, remove/kick, leave, policy, send, publish, consent)
description:
Mark, 2026-11-14 at the IETF 127 table: mimid should have a sideband (JSON / tool) path for every action, not only the protocol and JMAP surfaces. Today was blocked twice for lack of one: (1) no way to create a mimid-hosted room from outside the process (Room/create is a stub, mimid-1wgh.12.4; Hub::create_room is in-process only), so the 'room on mimid, Haven user invited' test couldn't run; (2) every client action at the table went through mimid-chat against Haven's JSON lane, because mimid has no equivalent of its own.

Scope to design (plan goes in this bead's design field for Mark's approval before sub-beads):
- Operator / hub actions on a running server: create a room (Hub::create_room), list rooms and users, remove or kick a user from a room (hub as external sender, a Remove proposal plus the participant_list update), ban, set room policy, publish KeyPackages for local users (what tools/interop/seed does offline), record and grant consent, issue dev bearer tokens.
- Client actions for test users whose identities mimid holds (the seed state): create a group, Add, Remove, leave (protocol-07 §3.5), send, and fetch key material through a room's hub. These are what mimid-chat does against Haven's hub; they need a mimid-side equivalent.
- Transport: a JSON API bound to localhost or a Unix socket, off by default and enabled per deployment, plus a CLI over it. It must be online: rooms live in the running hub's memory, so offline database edits like mimid-seed's don't take effect until a restart.
- Every action is logged with who asked, and none is reachable from the public listener.

Overlaps mimid-1wgh.32 (Admin CLI: users, tokens, list, ban, offline on SQLite). Decide whether .32 becomes the CLI half of this or is superseded. Related: mimid-1wgh.12.4 (Room/create) and mimid-1wgh.13 (mimid-agent).
design:
APPROVED by Mark 2026-11-15: client actions stay out of the server (1); optional local_token (2); mimid-1wgh.32 superseded by `mimid admin` (4).

Where it stands. The loopback listener (local.rs, `local_listen`, off by default, refuses a non-loopback address) already has GET /local/v1/hub-sender and POST /local/v1/rooms. mimid-chat's /host uses them, and it drives a mimid-hosted room as a client with --no-lane. So blocker (1) from 2026-11-14 is fixed, and (2) is fixed for test clients.

Proposal:

1. Split by who holds the keys. The server holds the hub's keys and its store, never a user's MLS keys (E2EE). So the sideband covers operator and hub actions only. Client actions (create a group, Add, Remove, leave, send, fetch key material) stay in a client: mimid-chat today, mimid-agent (mimid-1wgh.13) later. mimid does not hold test users' identities.

2. One transport. Extend the existing loopback JSON listener under /local/v1. No Unix socket for now; add one only if a deployment needs file-permission access control. Optional setting `local_token`: when set, every call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, so a shared host can still use it. Errors are RFC 9457 problems with type and status only, as elsewhere.

3. Routes (each a sub-bead, in this order):
   a. GET /local/v1/rooms, and GET /local/v1/rooms/{roomId}: hosted rooms with epoch, participants and roles, read from the hub. Read-only, needed by everything else.
   b. Users and tokens: POST /local/v1/users (create an account), POST /local/v1/users/{user}/tokens (issue a dev bearer token), GET /local/v1/users. These are the store calls that exist now (create_account, issue_token).
   c. Consent: GET /local/v1/consent (held requests and updates), so an operator can see what peers sent. Writing consent stays a protocol action.
   d. Remove or ban a user from a hosted room: the hub, as the room's external sender, sends a Remove proposal for the user's leaves plus the participant_list update (ban: role 1). The hub has no external-proposal path yet, so this is the one real piece of new protocol work; it goes last, with its own design note.
   Not proposed: room policy changes by the operator (policy is a member action under room-policy; an operator override would be a policy of its own), and KeyPackage publishing for users (a client action).

4. CLI: `mimid admin <command>` in the same binary, a thin client of these routes (it reads `local_listen` and `local_token` from the config). mimid-1wgh.32 (offline admin CLI on SQLite) becomes this and is closed as superseded: offline edits don't reach the running hub's memory.

5. Logging: each state-changing call logs at INFO with a stable event name, the route, the room or user, and the peer address. Reads log at DEBUG.

Decisions 2026-11-15 (Mark): (i) keep client actions out; (ii) optional local_token; (iii) close .32 into this.
close_reason: all six sub-beads done (local_token, rooms, users/tokens, consent, remove/ban, mimid admin)
